app.title: Promoter Screen Explorer
app.summary: A person opens a matrix of every candidate against every test condition. Colour shows how strongly each candidate performed against a reference, and the matrix also marks conditions never tested and conditions where quality-control exclusions removed some or all records. They narrow the matrix by family, ID search or timepoint, then click a candidate to open its profile: mean ± SD in each condition, the conditions it has not been tested in, and its flagged records. Up to six candidates can be added to a grouped bar comparison across chosen conditions. A QC panel switches each flag type on or off, and every view recomputes from that choice. Each chart panel can be saved as a PNG.

task.text: Answer which candidates have been tested in which conditions, how each did against a reference, and whether that holds once questionable records are excluded.

data.text: Replicate measurements of many candidates across several test conditions from two assay types. Each record is tagged with its experiment, a condition and an optional quality-control flag, and values are normalised to a reference candidate.
data.item: a candidate measured in one condition (a cell of the candidate × condition matrix), summarised from its replicate or per-animal records

stage.text: exploring pooled screening results after the assays have run, before choosing which candidates to take forward

mechanism.text: Tabs share one set of filters and one QC setting, and all summaries are recomputed from those. The coverage heatmap is the overview: clicking a row opens that candidate's profile, and the profile can add the candidate to a side-by-side bar comparison. Toggling a flag type in the QC review recomputes the reference-normalised means in every view.

field.text: promoter screening with reporter assays (flow cytometry in vitro, bioluminescence imaging in vivo) in AAV gene therapy

workflow.name: map which candidates were tested in which conditions and compare them against a reference

steps.here: A seeded static JSON of candidates and in vitro and in vivo records loads at start, and every QC flag type is excluded by default.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A candidate × condition matrix, grouped into in vitro cell lines and in vivo tissues, is coloured by log2 expression against the positive control. Dashed cells were never tested, hatched cells had every record excluded, outlined cells had some excluded, and the last column counts tested conditions.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Family dropdown, ID search box and an in vivo timepoint picker narrow the rows and set which timepoint is summarised.

Clicking a row or cell opens the candidate's profile: horizontal bars of mean ± SD per condition, a list of conditions not yet tested, and a table of its flagged records with included or excluded status.

'Add to comparison' sends the candidate to a grouped bar chart of up to six candidates. Condition chips toggle which conditions are shown, the bars carry error bars, and candidate–condition pairs with no data are listed under the chart.

A table of QC flag types shows how many in vitro records, in vivo records and candidates each flag affects. A switch per flag includes or excludes those records, and every summary is recomputed, including the in vivo reference mean.
Each chart panel has an 'Export PNG' button that saves a high-resolution image for slides.

distinctive: The matrix shows untested gaps as explicitly as measured values, so 'has this been tested here yet?' can be read straight off it.

Values are log2 fold change against a positive-control reference. In vivo signal is normalised per study, tissue and timepoint to the mean of the control animals that pass QC, so the reference itself changes when QC settings change.
QC exclusion works per flag type, not per record. Cells show whether a value rests on partly or fully excluded data, so the person can see how much a conclusion depends on questionable records.
Results from two assay types (in vitro cell lines and in vivo tissues at a chosen timepoint) are put on one shared scale in one matrix.
